brewing.notes: A safe starting point for black tea: Western style, water just off the boil.

description:
A selenium-rich black tea from Ningqiang in Hanzhong, Shaanxi, billed as the first black tea of the Hanzhong district and named for the old Jinniu road near its gardens.

Treat it as you would any black tea: water just off the boil, a few minutes in the pot, and a seller who can say where it was grown.
history: Local tea firms and research institutes developed it from 2009 over three years, and batch production began in 2012, the year it passed a municipal technical appraisal and won the Houji award at the Yangling agricultural fair. It was a departure for a province that had made only green tea. Little more is documented about it.
processing: Picked mainly as one bud with an opening leaf, then withered naturally, hand-rolled, moderately oxidised, shaped in a first firing and finished dry to lift the aroma.
harvest_season: Mainly from small-leaf population gardens above 800 metres; the plucking standard is one bud and one just-opening leaf.
appearance_dry: Tight, fine, curled strands, glossy dark with visible down.
taste_profile: High, lasting aroma; mellow, full and fresh on the palate.
vintage_note: Black teas are normally sold by harvest year and are best within a couple of years.
